subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Torsion Springs: Storing Rotational Energy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Torsion Springs: Storing Rotational Energy.

hook.text: A mousetrap snaps shut in milliseconds. All that speed comes from a twisted wire spring.

buildup.text: Torsion springs store energy when twisted. The restoring force is proportional to the angle of twist.

discovery.text: Clothespins use torsion springs. So do clipboard clips, wind-up toys, and self-closing hinges.

twist.text: A clock mainspring is a flat torsion spring. It unwinds slowly to release energy over hours.

climax.text: Ancient catapults used torsion springs made from twisted animal sinew to launch projectiles.

punchline.text: Twist a wire. Store an explosion. Release it on command.

quiz.question: How do torsion springs store energy?
options: By compressing coils together under heavy loads
By twisting around their axis and resisting the angular deformation
By stretching their length when pulled from both ends
